definition: A nucleophilic substitution in two steps: the carbon–halogen bond breaks first to give a carbocation (the slow, rate-determining step), then the nucleophile bonds to it; typical of tertiary halogenoalkanes, with rate $= k[\text{halogenoalkane}]$.

A nucleophilic substitution in one concerted step: the nucleophile bonds to carbon from the side opposite the halogen as the carbon–halogen bond breaks; typical of primary halogenoalkanes, with rate $= k[\text{halogenoalkane}][\text{nucleophile}]$.
An ion with a positive charge on a carbon atom that has only three bonds and six outer electrons, such as $\ce{(CH3)3C^+}$.
The flip of the three other groups on a carbon atom to the opposite side in an SN2 reaction, because the nucleophile attacks from the side opposite the leaving group.
